title: Effect of an administrative action
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean input word, let $B$ be a four-tape configuration for that input, and choose control states $q,q'$, a Boolean table word $T$, a table cursor $p\in\mathbb Z$, a state tape $\sigma\colon\mathbb Z\to\{0,1,\mathrm{blank}\}$ with cursor $s\in\mathbb Z$, table and state movements $d_t,d_s\in\{-1,0,1\}$, and an optional state-tape write $w\in\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{Option}(\{0,1\}))$. Applying the administrative action with target control $q'$, table movement $d_t$, state instruction $(w,d_s)$ to the evaluation configuration determined by $(B,q,T,p,\sigma,s)$ gives the evaluation configuration with control $q'$, table cursor $p+d_t$, state cursor $s+d_s$, and state tape unchanged if $w$ is absent or updated at $s$ to the value specified by $w$ if present.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean input word and four-tape base configuration
Boolean table and integer table cursor
Boolean-valued optional-symbol state tape and integer cursor
Table and state movements are signs
replaced:
Applying an administrative interpreter action --- one that moves the table
cursor by $d_t \in \{-1,0,1\}$, optionally writes a symbol at the state-tape
cursor, moves the state cursor by $d_s$, and passes to a control state $q'$
--- to an interpreter evaluation configuration changes exactly the two
designated cursors and, when a write is present, the state-tape cell at the
cursor; the input head, the mirrored data, and the accumulated output are
unchanged.
